title: New Delhi
short: The historic capital of India — home to UNESCO World Heritage monuments, grand Mughal architecture, bustling bazaars, and world-class luxury stays.
description: New Delhi is a captivating blend of ancient history and vibrant modernity. From imperial Mughal landmarks like Red Fort, Qutub Minar, and Humayun's Tomb to lush Mughal gardens, Lutyens' ceremonial avenues, and bustling spice markets of Chandni Chowk, Delhi offers an unforgettable travel experience for every explorer.

topPlaces.name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
topPlaces.description: A magnificent 17th-century red sandstone fortress built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. Serves as the historic seat of Mughal power and the site of India's annual Independence Day ceremony.

image.alt: Red Fort (Lal Qila) in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Qutub Minar
topPlaces.description: Standing at 72.5 meters, this world-renowned 12th-century brick minaret is decorated with intricate carving and Quranic inscriptions, surrounded by ancient ruins including the 1,600-year-old rust-resistant Iron Pillar.

image.alt: Qutub Minar in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Humayun's Tomb
topPlaces.description: The first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, built in 1570 for Mughal Emperor Humayun. Its symmetrical Charbagh garden and red sandstone-marble dome directly inspired the Taj Mahal.

image.alt: Humayun's Tomb in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: India Gate & Kartavya Path
topPlaces.description: A striking 42-meter high triumphal war memorial arch honoring 84,000 soldiers. Flanked by lush lawns, fountains, and the grand Kartavya Path leading to Rashtrapati Bhavan.
topPlaces.timings: Open 24 Hours (Best at sunset & evening illumination)

image.alt: India Gate & Kartavya Path in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Lotus Temple
topPlaces.description: Famous for its flower-like white marble petal design, this Bahá'í House of Worship is set amidst 26 acres of serene ponds and gardens, welcoming visitors of all faiths to meditate in silence.

image.alt: Lotus Temple in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Akshardham Temple
topPlaces.description: A colossal pink sandstone and white marble Hindu temple complex showcasing 10,000 years of Indian culture, featuring carved stone pillars, thematic boat rides, musical fountain shows, and sprawling gardens.

image.alt: Akshardham Temple in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Jama Masjid
topPlaces.description: Constructed by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1644 and 1656, this monumental red sandstone and white marble mosque can accommodate over 25,000 worshippers in its sprawling courtyard.

image.alt: Jama Masjid in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Chandni Chowk
topPlaces.description: Established in the 17th century by Princess Jahanara, Old Delhi's iconic market is world-famous for narrow heritage lanes, street food delicacies (paranthas, jalebis), spices (Khari Baoli), and textiles.

image.alt: Chandni Chowk in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Lodhi Garden
topPlaces.description: A peaceful 90-acre city park dotted with grand 15th-century mausoleums of the Sayyid and Lodi Dynasties, landscaped lawns, ancient stone bridges, and tranquil duck ponds.

image.alt: Lodhi Garden in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Hauz Khas Village & Fort
topPlaces.description: An eclectic urban contrast featuring 14th-century Khalji dynasty reservoir ruins, madrasa pavilions, and royal tombs paired directly with trendy art galleries, boutique shops, and rooftop cafes.

image.alt: Hauz Khas Village & Fort in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
topPlaces.description: One of the most prominent Sikh gurdwaras in Delhi, recognized by its gleaming gold dome, sacred Sarovar reflection pool, and community kitchen (Langar) feeding tens of thousands daily.

image.alt: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Agrasen ki Baoli
topPlaces.description: A hidden 60-meter long historical stepwell featuring 108 stone steps descending through three levels of arched alcoves in the heart of Connaught Place, protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

image.alt: Agrasen ki Baoli in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Rashtrapati Bhavan & Amrit Udyan
topPlaces.description: The official 340-room residence of the President of India, designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens. Features the famous 15-acre Amrit Udyan (Mughal Gardens) showcasing rare tulips, roses, and circular fountains.

image.alt: Rashtrapati Bhavan & Amrit Udyan in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Sunder Nursery
topPlaces.description: A UNESCO Award-winning 90-acre heritage park adjacent to Humayun's Tomb, featuring six restored 16th-century Mughal monuments, marble fountains, botanical garden collections, and tranquil lakes.

image.alt: Sunder Nursery in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Safdarjung Tomb
topPlaces.description: Built in 1754, this is the last garden-tomb of the Mughal architecture style in Delhi, featuring a high grand portal, ornate plasterwork, red sandstone facade, and expansive surrounding gardens.

image.alt: Safdarjung Tomb in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Purana Qila (Old Fort)
topPlaces.description: One of Delhi's oldest fortresses, with origins dating back to Indraprastha of the Mahabharata. Features massive 18-meter stone ramparts, Sher Mandal octagonal tower, and boating in the outer moat lake.

image.alt: Purana Qila (Old Fort) in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: National Museum
topPlaces.description: One of India's largest museums, housing over 200,000 rare artifacts spanning 5,000 years of civilization, including Harappan bronze dancing girl statues, ancient Buddhist relics, and Tanjore paintings.

image.alt: National Museum in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Jantar Mantar
topPlaces.description: Built in 1724 by Maharaja Jai Singh II of Jaipur, this astronomical observatory complex features 13 architectural instruments designed to compile astronomical tables and track sun & planetary movements.

image.alt: Jantar Mantar in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: Raj Ghat
topPlaces.description: A serene black marble memorial structure marking the spot of Mahatma Gandhi's cremation in 1948, surrounded by landscaped lawns, trees planted by world leaders, and an eternal flame.

image.alt: Raj Ghat in New Delhi

topPlaces.name: National Crafts Museum & Hastkala Academy
topPlaces.description: A delightful open-air village museum displaying traditional Indian handicrafts, rural village mud huts, carved wooden doors, live artisan demonstrations, and the popular Cafe Lota.

image.alt: National Crafts Museum & Hastkala Academy in New Delhi

title: Gurugram
short: The Millennium City of NCR — famous for Cyber Hub dining, luxury golf resorts, bird sanctuaries, and entertainment centers.
description: Gurugram is modern India's corporate and entertainment hub. Beyond its soaring glass skyscrapers, Cyber Hub nightlife, and Michelin-worthy dining, Gurugram offers nature retreats like Sultanpur Bird Sanctuary, Aravali Biodiversity Park, and luxury golf resorts.

topPlaces.name: DLF CyberHub
topPlaces.description: Premier food and nightlife destination featuring global cuisine and open plazas.

topPlaces.name: Sultanpur National Park
topPlaces.description: UNESCO-listed wetland sanctuary hosting over 250 species of migratory birds.

topPlaces.name: Kingdom of Dreams
topPlaces.description: Vibrant cultural complex showcasing live musical theater and Indian cuisine.

topPlaces.name: Heritage Transport Museum
topPlaces.description: India's first comprehensive museum dedicated to vintage cars, locomotives, and aviation.

topPlaces.name: Sheetla Mata Mandir
topPlaces.description: Revered 18th-century temple dedicated to Goddess Sheetla Devi.

topPlaces.name: Aravali Biodiversity Park
topPlaces.description: 380-acre restored forest park featuring native flora and walking trails.

title: Neemrana
short: A 15th-century heritage hill-fort getaway on Delhi-Jaipur highway — famous for zip-lining, stepwells, and romantic weekend stays.
description: Neemrana is an ancient historical town in Rajasthan's Alwar district, located just 120 km from New Delhi. Built in 1464 AD, the 14-tiered Neemrana Fort Palace carved into the Aravalli hills is one of India's premier heritage luxury resorts.

topPlaces.name: Neemrana Fort Palace
topPlaces.description: 15th-century 14-tiered hill fort featuring hanging gardens, pools, and ziplining.

topPlaces.name: Neemrana Baori
topPlaces.description: 9-storey deep subterranean stepwell built in the 18th century for royal caravans.

topPlaces.name: Siliserh Lake Palace
topPlaces.description: Picturesque 19th-century royal hunting lodge located on Siliserh Lake.

topPlaces.name: Hill Fort Kesroli
topPlaces.description: One of the oldest heritage forts in Rajasthan with panoramic countryside views.

title: Manesar & Damdama Lake
short: A serene countryside getaway near Delhi — famous for Damdama Lake boating, organic farmstays, Aravalli treks, and adventure camps.
description: Manesar & Damdama Lake form a relaxing rustic retreat just 45 km from Delhi. Surrounded by the rolling Aravalli ranges, Damdama Lake is one of Haryana's biggest natural lakes, offering boating, rock climbing, camping, and eco-resorts.

topPlaces.name: Damdama Lake
topPlaces.description: Scenic 3,000-acre lake under the Aravalli hills ideal for boating, kayaking, and camping.

topPlaces.name: Botanix Nature Resort
